coverageArticles.headline: How to Land 4,000 Planes During a Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: For four and a half hours, the sky above the United States emptied out. Normally, throughout the day and the night, thousands of planes are taking off, crisscrossing the country, and landing.

coverageArticles.headline: Scenes From the Nationwide Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare ground stop at all U.S. airports, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Across the country, departing flights were held for hours before the stop—attributed to a telecommunications outage—was lifted, disrupting travel plans for some 1.5 million people.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA ends hours-long nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop Friday night after hours of chaos and thousands of delays and cancellations. Why it matters: The effects of the rare and extreme move will likely ripple through the weekend, with travelers stranded and airlines' planes and crews out of position.

coverageArticles.headline: Duffy details timeline of ground stop, demands more FAA funding
coverageArticles.description: Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy gives the timeline of the paralyzing FAA ground stop, which left travelers across the country stranded for hours. Duffy says the issue was due to old communications systems.

coverageArticles.headline: Of Course Americans Blamed the Ground Stop on AI
coverageArticles.description: For many hours, the Federal Aviation Administration did not explain why it issued a national ground stop in the United States this afternoon. The agency described the cause only as a “ telecommunications outage ” and cited “ extraordinary circumstances ,” but failed to say more. So speculation abounded: Was the problem connected with the onboarding of a new AI route-selection system this week?

coverageArticles.headline: Airport Chaos Began Long Before the Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: Every civilian airplane in the United States has been told not to fly, owing to a nationwide FAA ground stop. As I write this, very little is known about the nature of the safety risk or the issue underlying it.

coverageArticles.headline: Stranded passenger in Las Vegas on nationwide ground stop: "Nobody has answers"
coverageArticles.description: Clara Pablo was trying to get home from Las Vegas to New York on Friday when the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop. She joined CBS News' to share her experience. Then, CBS Atlanta's Nakell Williams reports on the scene from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'

coverageArticles.description: An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. Lindsey Reiser anchors continuing coverage.
